tools.name: get_my_ip
tools.description: Return the public IP address (and ISP, ASN, location, timezone) of the caller as seen by FernTool. Note: for remote agents this is the IP of the machine calling the MCP server.

tools.name: lookup_ip
tools.description: Validate an IPv4/IPv6 address and return its version, scope (public/private/loopback/...), country, ASN and network owner (DB-IP Lite + IPtoASN data).

tools.name: validate_ip
tools.description: Check whether a string is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address and classify it.

tools.name: batch_lookup_ip
tools.description: Look up 1-100 IPv4/IPv6 addresses at once. Each result has version, scope, country, timezone, ASN, network owner and flags (is_tor, is_datacenter, provider).

tools.name: whois_lookup
tools.description: WHOIS via RDAP for a domain (registrar, created/expiry dates, status, nameservers, DNSSEC), an IP address (network name, range, owner org, country, abuse contact) or an ASN like AS13335.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Resolve DNS records for a domain via Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 DNS-over-HTTPS. Types: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, SOA (default: all).

tools.name: reverse_dns
tools.description: Reverse DNS (PTR) lookup for an IPv4/IPv6 address, with forward-confirmation check.

tools.name: subnet_calc
tools.description: IPv4/IPv6 CIDR subnet calculator: network, netmask, wildcard, broadcast, first/last usable host, total and usable addresses, block type.

tools.name: estimate_ai_cost
tools.description: Estimate token count and USD API cost of a text across major AI models (OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini), and whether it fits each context window. Token counts are approximate. Pass text, or tokens directly.

tools.name: make_qr_code
tools.description: Create a static QR code (never expires) for a URL, Wi-Fi string (WIFI:T:WPA;S:name;P:pass;;), mailto:, tel: or any text up to 2000 characters. Returns an SVG string plus a ferntool.com image URL that renders the same code.

tools.name: count_words
tools.description: Exactly count words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences and paragraphs in a text, with reading/speaking time and the most repeated words. Use this instead of estimating counts yourself.

tools.name: get_current_time
tools.description: Get the exact current date and time (you cannot know it otherwise). Returns Unix seconds and milliseconds, ISO 8601 in UTC and in the requested IANA time zone, weekday, ISO week and day of year.

tools.name: convert_timestamp
tools.description: Convert a Unix timestamp (seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds, auto-detected) to a readable date, or a date/time string (e.g. 2026-12-25 09:00, read in the given time zone unless it has its own offset) to a Unix timestamp. Also returns weekday, ISO week and how long ago or until.

tools.name: date_calc
tools.description: Exact calendar maths. With end: days between two dates (plus weeks, months+days, weekdays Mon-Fri, weekend days). With add_days/add_weeks/add_months/add_years (negative to subtract): the resulting date and weekday; business_days=true skips weekends. Use this instead of counting days yourself.

tools.name: convert_timezone
tools.description: Convert a time between time zones with daylight saving applied (you cannot do this reliably yourself). from/to accept IANA zones (Africa/Johannesburg), common abbreviations (SAST, EST, PST, GMT, CET, IST=India, CST=US Central) or big cities. Omit time for now. Returns each local date, time, UTC offs

tools.name: random_number
tools.description: Fair, cryptographically secure random integers (you cannot produce real randomness yourself). min and max are inclusive. unique=true for no repeats (raffles, lotto, picking winners). For a coin flip use min 0, max 1; for dice use min 1, max 6.

tools.name: pick_random
tools.description: Fairly pick random winners from a list, shuffle a list, or split people into random even teams, using a cryptographically secure generator (you cannot choose fairly at random yourself). Use for giveaways, raffles, "who goes first", random order or team splits. An item listed twice has twice the chan

tools.description: Check whether a DNS change has spread: asks the domain's own authoritative name server (when reachable) and 8 big public resolvers (Cloudflare, Google, OpenDNS, AdGuard, NextDNS, Control D, CleanBrowsing, AliDNS) over DoH, marks which are up to date, and gives the remaining cache time (TTL) of stale

tools.name: check_email_security
tools.description: Can someone fake (spoof) email from a domain? tools.name: check_website_status
tools.description: Is a website down? Resolves its DNS and loads the URL once (10 s timeout) from FernTool's Cloudflare edge, then returns verdict (up/down), reason (ok, blocked_bot, page_not_found, server_error, timeout, tls, dns_nxdomain...), HTTP status, response time, final URL after redirects and server country/n

tools.description: Where does a link really go? Follows a URL (short links like bit.ly, tracking links, QR code links) hop by hop without a browser: every redirect with status code (301/302/307/308/meta refresh), final URL and page title, plus warning signs (ends on a different site, domain registered < 30 days ago, p

tools.name: ai_service_status
tools.description: Live status of AI services (ChatGPT/OpenAI, Claude, Gemini API, GitHub Copilot, Perplexity, Cohere) read from their official status pages, cached ~60s. level is up, degraded, down or unknown.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_email_security, check_website_status · Private data: lookup_ip, whois_lookup, dns_lookup, estimate_ai_cost, check_email_security · Public sink: reverse_dns, subnet_calc, check_email_security.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_email_security, check_website_status · Private data: lookup_ip, whois_lookup, dns_lookup, estimate_ai_cost, check_email_security · Public sink: reverse_dns, subnet_calc, check_email_security

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
